title: Interactive Regression Builder MicroSim
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Data Science
description: Build a data set by clicking, dragging, and double-clicking points and watch the least-squares line, its equation, the meaning of its slope and intercept, R squared, RMSE, a residual plot, and a prediction update after every change.

educational.topic: Building and interpreting a simple linear regression model
learningObjectives: Students will be able to construct data sets with a required slope, strength of fit, or outlier, and interpret the fitted model's coefficients, R², RMSE, and predictions.
prerequisites: Residuals and the sum of squared errors

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Open-ended construction with immediate model feedback
keyQuestions: Where does an added point change the slope the most, near the middle of the x range or at the ends?
Can two very different data sets have the same regression line? Build an example.
Why is a prediction far outside the data range less trustworthy even when R² is high?
commonMisconceptions: A high R² means the predictions are reliable everywhere (the model is only supported inside the range of the data).
The intercept always has a real-world meaning (when x = 0 is far outside the data it is only where the line happens to cross the axis).
One unusual point cannot change the line much (a single point at the end of the x range can move the slope a lot).
An R² near 0 means the line was computed wrongly (it means x explains almost none of the variation in y).
assessmentOpportunities: Students build a data set of at least eight points whose fitted slope is between 2 and 3 and whose R² is above 0.8. They write the equation, interpret both coefficients, and explain whether a prediction at an x value of their choice is an interpolation or an extrapolation.
